generated_by: independent Python RFC 9180/JOSE fixture generator plus OpenSSL 3.6 ML-DSA-65; derived from the v1 fixture with target_asset_id as a uuid string
notes: Classical private scalars and the pinned ML-DSA key are test-only; never use these keys outside conformance tests.
All base64url values are unpadded. Standard-base64 fields are explicitly suffixed _b64.
The HPKE ciphertext is a real RFC 9180 base-mode seal, not a placeholder pattern.
Dial padding is one fixed CSPRNG sample captured once for this checked-in fixture, not a repeated-byte pattern.
Offline conformance validates the pinned test chain and status-window recipe; runtime pki-core must perform authoritative revocation/status checks and fail closed.
ML-DSA-65 is the authoritative tunnel principal-request path; Cloud and pki-core artifact signatures remain ES256.
This is the wendycloud.tunnel.v2 set: target_asset_id is a lowercase uuid string in both the request body and the signed descriptor target. Everything else in the contract is unchanged from v1.
The HPKE info/AAD/envelope and proof domain-separation strings deliberately keep their wendycloud.tunnel.v1/... spelling: they are frozen GrantKit constants, not package names.

The ML-DSA-65 principal key and its test chain are freshly minted for this set. The v1 private key was never checked in, so a v2 signature could not be produced under it; the leaf subject, SPIFFE SAN, serials, validity and extensions mirror the v1 chain exactly.
